proposal.residence_time_basis: Hydraulic liquid residence time calculated as stated reactor liquid hold-up (5.0 mL) divided by total liquid flow (0.500 mL/min).
proposal.light_setup: None. No light source or microwave source is available or proposed; this is a non-irradiated thermal flow screen.

streams.pump_role: Syringe pump A; sole liquid feed
streams.contents: A homogeneous DMF solution/suspension candidate containing aromatic bromide at 0.050 M (1.00 equiv), phenylboronic acid derivative, the batch-specified base, and the batch-specified palladium catalyst. The identities, boronic-acid equivalent, base equivalent, and catalyst loading were not provided and must be retained from the validated batch procedure rather than assumed.
streams.phase: liquid; use only if visually homogeneous and freely pumpable
streams.molar_equiv: Aromatic bromide = 1.00; all other reagent equivalents/loading = not specified in source batch protocol

proposal.mixer_type: None; one premixed feed is delivered by the only available pump.
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: The inventory contains one liquid pump and no listed mixer. Combining all batch components before charging the syringe avoids an unsupported two-stream metering operation. This approach is acceptable only if the complete feed remains homogeneous; no solid-slurry handling or in-line solids removal is proposed.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare the reaction mixture in DMF using the same reagent identities, boronic-acid/base stoichiometry, and Pd loading as the validated batch method; these values are missing from the supplied protocol and are not invented here.
Set aromatic bromide concentration to 0.050 M, giving 16.0 mL of feed for a 1.60 mmol aromatic-bromide experiment.
Confirm that the complete feed is homogeneous, free-flowing, and remains so during the anticipated run. Do not run a visibly settling or precipitating feed in the 1.0 mm ID coil.
Charge the premixed feed to Syringe pump A and connect it directly to the 5 mL PFA coil using the listed 1.0 mm ID PFA tubing.

Maintain the reactor at exactly 50.0 C. The inventory does not identify the temperature-control implementation; this condition is a required facility/setpoint capability, not an additional selected flow component.
Install the 5 bar BPR downstream of the coil and direct the BPR outlet to collection.
At 0.500 mL/min, allow at least one reactor volume (10.0 min) after establishing stable flow before collecting the residence-time-defined product fraction.
post_reactor_steps: Collect the effluent after the 5 bar BPR once the 10.0 min reactor hold-up has elapsed.
Analyze conversion and biaryl yield against the microwave-batch result; no unlisted quench, separation, or purification hardware is prescribed.
At run completion, stop collection, reduce pump flow to zero, and allow controlled depressurization through the installed BPR before disconnecting tubing.
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a Suzuki-type Pd coupling thermal comparison at the validated batch temperature, not a claim that microwave heating is reproduced. Microwave irradiation can change heating profile and apparent rate even at the same nominal bulk temperature. DMF, boronic-acid derivatives, inorganic bases, and Pd catalysts can form precipitates; a clear premix is a mandatory operational gate because the available equipment has no dedicated slurry pump, filter, or second feed channel. At the selected aromatic-bromide concentration and flow, substrate throughput is 0.025 mmol/min; processing 1.60 mmol requires 64.0 min of feed delivery, excluding the 10.0 min start-up hold-up.

stage_parameters.reagent_stoichiometry: Use the unspecified but validated batch stoichiometry and Pd loading; do not infer values from the reported yield.

stage_parameters.collection_basis: Collect only after one calculated reactor volume has passed.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: 10.0 min preserves the validated batch reaction duration as the first thermal-flow screen.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 5.0 mL / 10.0 min = 0.500 mL/min; this is above the pump minimum of 0.010 mL/min and below its 5.0 mL/min maximum.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Exactly 50.0 C, as required and within the PFA coil 80 C rating.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.050 M is deliberately conservative to reduce the likelihood of precipitation and excessive pressure drop in a 1.0 mm ID coil. It is not claimed to match an unreported batch concentration.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: The available 5 bar BPR is the lower available setting and provides controlled backpressure while remaining below the 20 bar pump and tubing ratings.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: The 5.0 mL coil is selected because it gives the desired 10.0 min residence time at a practical 0.500 mL/min with the sole pump.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_inlet_min: Set to 0.0 min because no quantified pre-reactor tubing hold-up was supplied; stated residence time refers only to the reactor channel.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No optical or microwave apparatus exists in the inventory, so none is proposed.
reasoning_per_field.streams: One stream is required because only one pump is available; reagent splitting would require unsupported simultaneous metering.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: Premixing eliminates the need for a tee or static mixer not listed in inventory.

proposal.literature_analogies: Thermal continuous-flow Suzuki-Miyaura couplings commonly use short PFA coils, polar aprotic solvents, Pd catalysts, a base, and several-minute residence times. However, no source-specific analogue was supplied for this exact substrate/base/catalyst system, and no direct equivalence between microwave and conventional thermal flow is assumed.
safety_flags: Do not exceed the 20 bar maximum pressure of Syringe pump A or the listed PFA tubing. The 5 bar BPR setting leaves nominal pressure margin, but pressure drop from any solids or blockage is unverified.
Use only a homogeneous, non-settling feed. Any precipitation, settling, rising backpressure, or loss of flow is a stop condition.
DMF and Pd-containing effluent require appropriate chemical handling and waste segregation.
No gas is used: inlet gas flow is 0 sccm and pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow is 0 mL/min.
The absence of microwave hardware means the 91% microwave-batch yield cannot be treated as a validated expected flow yield.
Exactly 50.0 C operation requires a verified temperature-control capability for the coil; no unlisted heating device is selected in this proposal.
proposal.confidence: Moderate for hydraulic feasibility and constraint compliance; low-to-moderate for chemical performance until the missing reagent identities/loadings and feed solubility are confirmed and the non-microwave thermal comparison is tested.

disposition_rationale: A single-premixed-stream thermal flow screen is compatible with the one available syringe pump, 5 mL PFA coil, 5 bar BPR, and all stated flow/pressure/temperature limits. The proposed 0.500 mL/min flow through the 5.0 mL coil gives the batch-matched 10.0 min in-channel residence time at exactly 50.0 C. SCREEN rather than EXECUTE is required because the batch result used microwave irradiation, whereas no microwave or light source is available, and because the identities, equivalents, catalyst loading, and solubility of the base/catalyst are not supplied. This is therefore a thermal comparability experiment, not a validated replication of the microwave batch reaction.
